title: Ang Thong 2-Day Itinerary 2026 — Temples, Crafts & River | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night Ang Thong itinerary in Thailand: the giant Buddha at Wat Muang, the reclining Buddha at Wat Khun Inthapramun, the Ekkarat drum village, Bang Sadet court dolls, and riverside temples on the Chao Phraya — with a full timeline, boat-noodle stops, and where to stay overnight.
keywords: Ang Thong 2-day itinerary, Ang Thong travel plan, Wat Muang Ang Thong, Ekkarat drum village, Bang Sadet court dolls, where to stay in Ang Thong
h1:
Ang Thong 2 Days, 1 Night
Temples · Craft Villages · The Chao Phraya
intro: Ang Thong is a small province less than two hours' drive from Bangkok. You can see the giant Buddha and the reclining Buddha in a single day, but with two days and one night you get to slip in the things many people miss — the Ekkarat drum-making village, the Bang Sadet court dolls, and quiet temples along the Chao Phraya river without rushing. We put the temples and giant Buddha on day one, stay one night in town, then spend day two on crafts and the riverside, so the loop flows without backtracking.

blocks.html: Ang Thong is about 100 km from Bangkok. Take the Asia Highway (Route 32) and you'll be there in roughly an hour and a half. The sights are spread across different districts and public transport is awkward to piece together, so this plan assumes you're driving yourself. Staying one night means you don't have to cram everything into a single day — you can walk slowly, chat with the drum makers, watch the women shaping the dolls, and sit down to a bowl of boat noodles in peace, rather than rushing a day trip.

items: Day 1 — Temples and the giant Buddha around Wiset Chai Chan and Pho Thong, finishing in town for the night.
Day 2 — The Pa Mok crafts: the drum village, the court dolls, and a Chao Phraya riverside temple, before heading back to Bangkok.
Total distance — Bangkok to Ang Thong and back is about 220 km, plus roughly 80 km looping around the province over two days.
Budget per person — Accommodation, fuel, food, and merit offerings come to about 1,200–2,000 THB (most temples don't charge admission).
What to wear — You'll visit several temples, so wear a top with sleeves, trousers or a skirt that covers the knees, and comfortable walking shoes.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Wat Muang is open 06:00–18:00, Wat Khun Inthapramun roughly 08:00–17:00, and the Bang Sadet court-doll centre roughly 09:00–16:00. Putting the craft villages on day two, mid-morning, lines up nicely with when the makers start work — that's when you'll see the most of the process.

blocks.text: Day 1 timeline — giant Buddha, reclining Buddha, food along the way

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Temple day, starting with the giant Buddha at Wat Muang

items.activity: Leave Bangkok and get on the Asia Highway (Route 32)
items.note: Set off a little early to beat the traffic. Stop for a restroom break or coffee at a service station on the way if you need to.

items.activity: Arrive at Wat Muang in Wiset Chai Chan and pay respects to Luang Pho Yai, the largest Buddha image in Thailand
items.note: The lap is about 62 m wide and the figure stands roughly 93 m tall. Open 06:00–18:00, no admission. Come early while the sun is still soft — the white Buddha against the blue sky photographs beautifully.

items.activity: Walk the grounds of Wat Muang — the heaven-and-hell tableau and the lotus-petal glass wall
items.note: There's a lot of detail here, so take your time and wander; no need to hurry.

items.activity: Drive into Ang Thong town for a late-morning bowl of boat noodles
items.note: Town has several well-known shops. Small bowls start around 20 THB, so it's easy to order a few.

items.activity: Head to Pho Thong district to see the reclining Buddha at Wat Khun Inthapramun
items.note: This open-air reclining Buddha is about 50 m long and dates back to the Sukhothai era. Open roughly 08:00–17:00.

items.activity: Stop at Wat Ton Son in town to pay respects to Somdet Phra Si Mueang Thong
items.note: A large gilded, lacquered metal Buddha image right by the Chao Phraya — an easy stop.

items.activity: Check in at your hotel in town, rest up, and recharge
items.note: Town has both in-town hotels and riverside resorts to choose from.

items.activity: Stroll along the Chao Phraya in the evening and find dinner in town
items.note: Evenings by the river are cool and breezy — a good time for sunset photos.

blocks.text: Boat noodles and where to eat on day one

blocks.html: When people think of food in Ang Thong, boat noodles come to mind first — a rich, deep broth in small, cheap bowls, and ordering several at a time is completely normal. These are the shops locals and travellers mention most often, picked from real reviews.

items.name: Ruea Thong Boat Noodles (near the monument)
items.blurb: A big place with plenty of seating and a steady stream of customers, serving both tom yum and clear-broth boat noodles. The broth is well balanced, the small bowls are easy on the wallet, and it's a good late-morning stop along the route.
items.meta: Boat noodles · small bowls from about ฿20

items.name: Tiao Ruea Yutya (in front of Ang Thong Hospital)
items.blurb: A local favourite with a punchy broth that needs no extra seasoning, in nam tok, tom yum, and clear-broth styles. The standout side is the braised-pork rice stir-fried with kaffir lime leaf. Open roughly 08:30–17:00.
items.meta: Boat noodles · Pho Sa, Mueang district

items.name: Sane Ang Thong Boat Noodles
items.blurb: A local boat-noodle shop with tom yum, clear broth, and pad thai at reasonable prices — handy for a quick meal before moving on to the next temple.
items.meta: Boat noodles & pad thai · in town

items.name: Por Prathip Boat Noodles
items.blurb: On the Ang Thong–Pa Mok road in Sala Daeng, right on the route to and from Pa Mok — a convenient stop on day two.
items.meta: Boat noodles · Ang Thong–Pa Mok road

items.name: Tom Yum Noodle Shop at the Pa Mok Bend
items.blurb: A homey shop right on the bend toward Pa Mok, known for tom yum noodles with minced pork, offal, soft-boiled egg, and crispy wontons, at easy prices.
items.meta: Tom yum noodles · on the way to Pa Mok

blocks.title: On accommodation
blocks.html: Ang Thong town runs from in-town hotels in the low hundreds of baht up to riverside resorts. Most average rooms run around 500–1,100 THB per night depending on the season. If you want the riverside atmosphere, book ahead — rooms with a river view are limited.

blocks.text: Day 2 timeline — Pa Mok crafts and the Chao Phraya riverside

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Craft day — Ekkarat drums, Bang Sadet dolls, riverside temple

items.activity: Check out, grab breakfast in town, then drive south to Pa Mok district
items.note: Pa Mok is south of town, about a 20–30 minute drive.

items.activity: Arrive at the drum-making village in Ekkarat sub-district, behind Pa Mok market, to watch the makers stretch the hide, hammer the pegs, and tune the pitch
items.note: Walking around is free — it's a direct visit to the makers' workshops. By mid-morning they're at work, so you'll see the steps clearly, and you can try tapping out a tune.

items.activity: Drive on to Bang Sadet sub-district to see the Bang Sadet court-doll centre
items.note: Less than 10 minutes away. Open roughly 09:00–16:00. Watch the women mould, demould, and paint on the spot — at certain times you can try shaping a doll yourself.

items.activity: Stop at Wat Pa Mok Worawihan to see the Ayutthaya-era reclining Buddha, about 24 m long, beside the Chao Phraya
items.note: It's in the same district, and you can feed the fish along the river.

items.activity: Lunch around Pa Mok — stop at Por Prathip Boat Noodles on the way back
items.note: It's right on the Ang Thong–Pa Mok road, so it's on the way.
You'll be home around 15:30–16:00, ahead of the evening rush.

blocks.html: Both the Ekkarat drums and the Bang Sadet dolls come from the same root: Pa Mok villagers looking for income beyond rice farming, building on what was already around them. The Ekkarat side works with wood and the maker's skill; the Bang Sadet side uses the clay from the riverbank. Both became handicrafts that have supported their communities for generations, and a distinctive image of the province that you won't find elsewhere.

items.name: Ban Ekkarat Drum Making
items.blurb: Woodwork and hide work — listen to the drums, watch the makers hammer the pegs in real time. Everything from the klong that and long drums to taiko and djembe. Souvenirs start in the low hundreds; great for anyone into craft and music.

items.name: Bang Sadet Court-Doll Centre
items.blurb: Hand-painted clay figures in a Thai-style house by the Chao Phraya, from a royal-initiative project, shaped into scenes of old Thai life. Gentler and more delicate — good to bring both kids and adults.

blocks.title: A note on souvenirs
blocks.html: The Bang Sadet figures are entirely handmade, so no two are exactly alike — if you find one you love, grab it, because the next batch may not have the same pose. For the Ekkarat drums, if you want a large one or a special order, call the shop ahead, as some take several days to make. Bring cash to both places; it's easier.

blocks.text: Extra stops if you have time to spare

items.name: Ban Bang Chao Cha, basketry
items.blurb: A bamboo-basketry craft community in Pho Thong district, another of Ang Thong's well-known crafts. Stop to look and pick up basketwork you'll actually use.

items.name: San Chao Rong Thong Market
items.blurb: An old market in Wiset Chai Chan district with local food and traditional sweets — a good stop for a bite if you're passing through the Wiset Chai Chan side.

items.name: Wat Tha Sutthawat
items.blurb: A Chao Phraya riverside temple in Pa Mok district with mural paintings and a quiet riverside setting. An easy add-on after Wat Pa Mok.

blocks.text: Getting there and shaping the trip

items: Self-drive — The easiest option. Take Route 32 (the Asia Highway), then turn off into the province. The main temples and town have plenty of parking.

Van / bus — There are services from Mo Chit to Ang Thong town, but within the province you'll need to switch to a songthaew or charter a vehicle, which isn't great if you want to loop through several districts.
Pair it with Ayutthaya — Ang Thong sits right next to Ayutthaya, and Pa Mok is to the south, very close to it. With a bit more time, a two-province trip fits together neatly.
Avoid long holidays — Wat Muang gets very busy during festivals. For easy photos and easy bookings, a weekday is better.

faq.q: What can you do in Ang Thong over 2 days and 1 night?
faq.a: Day one focuses on temples — Luang Pho Yai at Wat Muang, the reclining Buddha at Wat Khun Inthapramun, and Wat Ton Son — then a night in town. Day two is the Pa Mok crafts: the Ekkarat drum village, the Bang Sadet court-doll centre, and Wat Pa Mok by the Chao Phraya. The loop covers it all without rushing.

faq.q: Why stay overnight when you can see it in a day?
faq.a: In one day you can see the giant Buddha and the reclining Buddha, but if you want to add the craft villages and riverside temples without hurrying, staying one night lets you walk slowly, chat with the drum makers, watch the women shaping the dolls, and enjoy your boat noodles. It suits anyone who doesn't want to drive far and rush it all in a single day.

faq.q: Where should you stay overnight in Ang Thong?
faq.a: Ang Thong town has both in-town hotels in the low hundreds of baht and resorts along the Chao Phraya. Most rooms average around 500–1,100 THB per night depending on the season. If you want a river-view room, book ahead — they're limited.

faq.q: Are the drum village and the court-doll village far apart?
faq.a: Not at all. Both are in Pa Mok district, and the drive from the Ekkarat drum village to the Bang Sadet court-doll centre is under 10 minutes, so you can do them back to back in a single morning. Both are free to visit.

faq.q: How long does it take to drive to Ang Thong from Bangkok?
faq.a: About an hour and a half with no traffic, via Route 32 (the Asia Highway), a distance of roughly 100 km. The sights are spread across different districts, so driving yourself is the easiest way to loop around.
